text: This policy sets the security requirements for Acme SaaS Ltd ("Acme") and the Acme Workspace platform, including the Acme Assist AI features. It applies to all employees, contractors and systems that store or process customer data.

The Head of Security owns the information security programme and reports to the CTO. A Security Steering Committee (CTO, Head of Security, Head of Engineering, Data Protection Officer) meets quarterly to review risks, incidents and policy exceptions. All security policies are reviewed at least annually.

Acme holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification. The certificate scope covers the Acme Workspace platform and supporting operations at the London office. Acme completes an annual SOC 2 Type II audit covering the Security, Availability and Confidentiality trust services criteria. The SOC 2 report is available to customers and prospects under NDA.

Background checks are carried out on all new hires before their start date, to the extent permitted by local law. All staff sign confidentiality agreements. Security awareness training is completed at onboarding and annually thereafter, and phishing simulations are run quarterly.

Access follows the principle of least privilege. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all workforce accounts. Production access is granted through SSO with just-in-time elevation, is time-limited, and every session is logged. Access to production systems is reviewed quarterly. Leavers have access revoked within 24 hours of their departure. Customer-facing identity controls are described in the Identity, SSO & SCIM document (IAM).

Data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher, with TLS 1.3 preferred. Customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 using AWS Key Management Service. Encryption keys are managed by Acme and rotated annually.

Dependencies are scanned automatically on every build, and container images are scanned before deployment. Remediation targets from discovery are: critical within 7 days, high within 30 days, medium within 90 days. An independent third party performs a penetration test of the application and infrastructure at least annually. An executive summary of the latest test is available to customers under NDA.

All code changes require peer review before merge. Static application security testing (SAST) runs in the CI pipeline. Development, staging and production environments are separated, and customer data is never used in non-production environments.
Security-relevant logs from infrastructure and applications are centralised and retained for 12 months. Alerts are monitored by an on-call engineering rota 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
All company laptops are centrally managed, use full-disk encryption and run endpoint detection and response (EDR) software. Personal devices may not be used to access production systems.
Exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Head of Security, recorded in the risk register, and reviewed at least every six months.

This statement covers Acme Assist, the generative AI features in Acme Workspace: document summarisation, meeting-minutes drafting, and natural-language search across a customer's workspace. Acme does not use AI to make automated decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects on individuals.

Acme Assist uses third-party foundation models accessed via API. Acme does not train its own foundation models. The current model providers are listed in the Sub-processor List (SUB). Model details, intended use and limitations are documented in the Acme Assist Model Card (MC).

section_title: Use of customer data for training
text: Customer data is never used to train, fine-tune or otherwise improve any AI model, whether Acme's or a third party's. Our agreements with model providers prohibit them from using customer prompts or outputs for training. Model providers retain prompts and outputs for no more than 30 days for abuse monitoring only, under zero-data-retention terms where offered.

AI features are disabled by default for new customer tenants. A customer workspace administrator must opt in at tenant level, and can turn Acme Assist off at any time. Administrators can also restrict AI features to specific user groups.

Acme Assist only retrieves content the requesting user already has permission to see. Permissions are enforced at retrieval time, before any content is sent to a model. Content is never shared between customer tenants.
All AI outputs are presented as drafts that a user must review, edit or accept. Acme Assist cannot send, publish or approve content on its own. AI-generated content is labelled in the user interface.

An AI Governance Group (Head of AI Product, Head of Security, Data Protection Officer, General Counsel) approves every new AI feature and any change of model provider. Approval requires a completed AI impact assessment covering privacy, security, fairness and misuse risks. The group meets monthly.

Acme's AI governance programme is aligned with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage). Acme is working towards ISO/IEC 42001 and has completed a gap assessment. Acme maintains an inventory of all AI systems in use, including internal tools.

Acme has assessed Acme Assist against the EU AI Act and classified it as a limited-risk system, as it is not used for any purpose listed in Annex III. Acme meets the transparency obligations by informing users when they interact with AI and by labelling AI-generated content.

Before release, every AI feature is evaluated against a held-out test set for accuracy and hallucination rate, and undergoes internal adversarial testing for prompt injection and data leakage. In production, Acme monitors user feedback (thumbs up/down) and samples outputs for quality review each month.

Customers may not use Acme Assist for unlawful purposes, to generate harmful content, or to make decisions about individuals without human review. Abuse may result in AI features being suspended for the tenant.

Acme Assist is a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system. When a user makes a request, Acme Assist retrieves relevant passages from the user's workspace, passes them to a large language model with a system prompt, and returns a draft with links to the source documents.
Acme Assist is intended to help professional users summarise long documents, draft meeting minutes from notes, and find information in their workspace. It is intended for use in English.
Acme Assist is not intended for legal, medical or financial advice, for decisions about employment or creditworthiness, or for any use where outputs are relied on without human review.

Generation uses a third-party large language model provided by the model providers listed in SUB. Retrieval uses a third-party text embedding model. Acme pins model versions and tests every version change before rollout.

Each release is evaluated on an internal benchmark of 500 workspace tasks. Metrics include factual consistency with source documents, citation accuracy and refusal behaviour. Release requires factual consistency of at least 95% on the benchmark.

Acme Assist can produce inaccurate or incomplete summaries, particularly for long tables, scanned documents and non-English content. It may miss information in documents the user cannot access. Outputs should always be checked against the source.

Mitigations include permission-aware retrieval, source citations in every answer, a system prompt that instructs the model to say when information is not available, input filtering for known prompt-injection patterns, and output length limits.
Customer content is retained for the duration of the subscription. Customers can delete individual items at any time; deleted items move to a recycle bin and are permanently deleted after 30 days.

On termination, customers have 30 days to export their data. Customer data is then deleted from production systems within 30 days, and from backups within a further 35 days as backups expire. A certificate of deletion is available on request.
Production databases are backed up daily. Backups are encrypted, stored in a separate AWS region within the same jurisdiction, and retained for 35 days.

Acme Assist prompts and outputs are stored in the customer's tenant for 90 days to provide conversation history, then deleted automatically. Administrators can shorten this period or disable history. See AIG-3 for model provider retention.
Application and security logs are retained for 12 months. Logs are designed to exclude customer content.
Retention may be suspended where required by law or a legal hold, and the customer will be informed where legally permitted.

Every sub-processor undergoes a security and privacy assessment before onboarding and is reviewed annually. All sub-processors are bound by a data processing agreement with obligations at least as protective as Acme's customer DPA.
Acme gives customers at least 30 days' notice of any new sub-processor by email to subscribed contacts. Customers may object on reasonable data-protection grounds during the notice period.

Where a sub-processor processes personal data outside the UK or EEA, Acme relies on the UK International Data Transfer Addendum and EU Standard Contractual Clauses. No current sub-processor processes customer content outside the UK or EEA.
This policy covers security incidents, personal data breaches and AI incidents affecting Acme systems or customer data.

- SEV1: confirmed breach of customer data or full platform outage. - SEV2: suspected breach, or major degradation affecting multiple customers. - SEV3: limited impact, contained, no customer data affected.
Incidents follow five phases: detection, triage, containment, eradication and recovery, and post-incident review. An incident commander is appointed for every SEV1 and SEV2 incident.

Acme notifies affected customers of a confirmed personal data breach without undue delay, and in any case within 48 hours of confirmation. Notification includes the nature of the breach, likely consequences and the measures taken.

AI incidents include outputs that expose data across permission boundaries, successful prompt injection, or materially harmful outputs. AI incidents are handled under this policy, with the Head of AI Product joining the response team. Acme can disable Acme Assist globally or per tenant within 15 minutes.
The incident response plan is tested at least annually through a tabletop exercise. Post-incident reviews are completed within 10 business days of every SEV1 and SEV2 incident.
Acme Workspace is hosted on Amazon Web Services. The primary region is London (eu-west-2). Backups and disaster recovery are in Ireland (eu-west-1). Acme does not operate its own data centres.
All customer content is stored in the UK, with backup copies in the EU. Acme does not currently offer hosting in other regions.

Acme Workspace is a multi-tenant application. Each customer's data is logically separated by a tenant identifier enforced at the application and database layers, and every query is scoped to a single tenant.

Production runs in private subnets behind a web application firewall and load balancer. Administrative access is only possible through an SSO-protected bastion. DDoS protection is provided by AWS Shield.

The platform runs across three availability zones in the primary region. Target availability is 99.9% monthly, excluding scheduled maintenance. Current status and incident history are published on a public status page.

Acme Assist runs as a separate service inside the same AWS environment. Prompts are sent to the model provider over TLS through a private gateway that strips account identifiers and logs request metadata only. Embedding indexes are stored per tenant.
Acme Workspace supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect single sign-on with any standards-compliant identity provider. Administrators can enforce SSO for all users in the tenant.
SCIM 2.0 provisioning and de-provisioning is supported on Enterprise plans. Removing a user in the identity provider revokes their access to Acme Workspace on the next sync.

Where SSO is not used, passwords must be at least 12 characters and are checked against known-breached password lists. Passwords are hashed using bcrypt. Users can enable MFA via authenticator app, and administrators can make it mandatory.

Acme Workspace provides role-based access control with Owner, Admin, Member and Guest roles, plus document-level permissions. Administrators can view an audit log of logins, permission changes and exports.
Session timeout is configurable by administrators between 1 hour and 30 days. Administrators can terminate all active sessions for a user.

For customer content, the customer is the data controller and Acme is the data processor. Acme processes customer personal data only on the customer's documented instructions, as set out in the Data Processing Agreement (DPA).
Acme's processing is designed to comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and EU GDPR. Acme is registered with the UK Information Commissioner's Office.
Acme has appointed a Data Protection Officer, who can be contacted at privacy@acme-saas.example.

Acme provides tools that let customers export, correct and delete personal data to respond to data subject requests. If Acme receives a request directly, it forwards it to the customer without undue delay.

Acme carries out data protection impact assessments for new processing likely to result in high risk, including every new AI feature. Acme will provide reasonable assistance to customers completing their own DPIAs.
Acme maintains records of processing activities as required by Article 30 of the UK GDPR.
Acme Workspace is not designed for special category personal data. Customers are responsible for deciding whether to store such data in the platform.
For a full loss of the primary region, the recovery time objective (RTO) is 8 hours and the recovery point objective (RPO) is 24 hours.
Recovery uses encrypted backups replicated to the Ireland region (see DR-3). Infrastructure is defined as code so the platform can be rebuilt in the recovery region.
A disaster recovery restore test is performed at least annually, and backup restores are tested quarterly. Results are reviewed by the Security Steering Committee.
Acme staff can work fully remotely, and no critical business process depends on a single office or a single person.
